definitions.explanation: A round, open-topped container traditionally made of wood, used for carrying water, bathing, or storage. In modern use, also refers to plastic basins and tubs.

examples.japanese: {風呂|ふろ}{桶|おけ}でお{湯|ゆ}をかけた。
examples.english: I poured hot water with a bath bucket.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{桶|おけ}に{水|みず}を{入|い}れて{花|はな}を{生|い}けた。
examples.english: I put water in a wooden tub and arranged flowers in it.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}はこの{地域|ちいき}の{職人|しょくにん}が{手作|てづく}りの{桶|おけ}を{作|つく}っていた。
examples.english: In the old days, craftsmen in this area used to make handcrafted wooden buckets.

notes:
USAGE:
Traditionally refers to wooden containers made by coopers ({桶屋|おけや}). In modern everyday life, most commonly encountered as {風呂|ふろ}{桶|おけ} (bath bucket used for scooping water in Japanese-style bathing). Also appears in the well-known proverb {風|かぜ}が{吹|ふ}けば{桶屋|おけや}が{儲|もう}かる (when the wind blows, the bucket-maker profits — a chain of unlikely cause and effect).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {風呂|ふろ}{桶|おけ}: bath bucket
- {木|き}{桶|おけ}: wooden bucket
- {桶屋|おけや}: bucket-maker, cooper
- {寿司|すし}{桶|おけ}: sushi serving tub

SIMILAR WORDS:
- バケツ: bucket (Western-style, usually metal or plastic, with a handle)
